ticket.title: Product page reads stall when several shoppers browse at once
ticket.symptom: One shopper can open a product promptly. When several product reads overlap, responses stretch and a few clients give up. The last change to this sandbox read path rebuilds the catalog snapshot on every request while holding the catalog lock.
ticket.ask: Show the slowdown from evidence collected in the sandbox, then propose a change an engineer can validate here before anything is shipped.
ticket.disclaimer: This ticket was written for the demo. It is not a Jira issue, and it was not synced from a tracker.

diagnosis.methodLabel: Rule-based sandbox demonstration — not live model inference
diagnosis.title: Exclusive catalog lock is serializing overlapping reads
diagnosis.summary: Under the same load (32 requests, concurrency 8, client timeout 5000 ms, scheduled read 80 ms), incident p95 client latency was 650.6 ms and baseline p95 was 93.24 ms. Mean lock wait was 494.29 ms in the incident samples and 0 ms in the baseline samples. The deepest incident lock queue was 7 waiters. All three rules fired. They point at the read path that holds the exclusive lock for the 80 ms timer.

rules.title: Incident p95 client latency is at least double the baseline and 40 ms higher
rules.threshold: incident p95 >= baseline p95 × 2 and incident p95 − baseline p95 >= 40 ms
rules.observed: Baseline p95 93.24 ms, incident p95 650.6 ms.

rules.title: Incident mean lock wait is at least 25 ms and at least 4× the baseline
rules.threshold: incident mean lock wait >= 25 ms and >= max(5 ms, baseline mean × 4)
rules.observed: Baseline mean lock wait 0 ms, incident mean lock wait 494.29 ms.

rules.title: Incident lock queue reaches at least 3 waiters and exceeds baseline
rules.threshold: incident max lock waiters >= 3 and greater than baseline
rules.observed: Baseline max lock waiters 0, incident max lock waiters 7.

uncertainties: This diagnosis is a deterministic rule set in src/lib/diagnosis.ts. No language model was called, and no model credential is configured.
The ticket shown beside this run is a seeded example. It did not arrive from Jira or any other tracker.
Every latency, lock-wait, queue, log, and trace figure is from this local catalog process on this run. None of them is a production SLO, a customer impact number, or a savings claim.
The catalog is a small original sandbox. The OpenTelemetry Astronomy Shop is not running, and these traces were not imported from it.
The slow read is a timer inside this process. It stands in for an expensive critical section. It is not a profiler capture from a customer system.
The same timer runs in baseline mode, outside the lock. The comparison isolates lock placement. It does not measure a second, unknown production bug.
Approving the proposal only flips this sandbox process to the outside-lock placement and reruns the load. That check is not a production verification.

proposal.title: Move the catalog read outside the exclusive lock
proposal.summary: Incident mode holds one exclusive lock for the whole slow read, so overlapping callers queue. The sandbox can instead copy the in-memory product under a short lock and run the same timed read after the lock is released. That is a hypothesis to check in this process. It is not a patch applied to a production repository, and it has not been shown to fix anything outside this demo.
proposal.sandboxChange: After engineer confirmation, the demo sends POST /admin/mode {"mode":"remediated"} to the catalog process on 127.0.0.1 only.
validationPlan: Use the same request count, concurrency, timeout, and product mix as the investigation load.
Switch the local catalog to remediated mode only after the confirmation control in this page sends APPLY_SANDBOX_REMEDIATION.
Repeat the load against that local process.
Compare client latency, lock wait, and lock-queue depth with the incident samples kept from this investigation.
Leave the result labeled as a sandbox check. Do not open a pull request, write to a tracker, or deploy.
proposal.boundary: Nothing in the catalog process changes until an engineer confirms it here. Reset returns the catalog to baseline mode. The demo has no path that writes outside this machine.
